claims.claim: In 2024, Stonehenge's Altar Stone was traced to Scotland.

claims.note: Clarke 2024 (online 14 Aug 2024), title 'A Scottish provenance for the Altar Stone of Stonehenge'; abstract: detrital ages show 'a remarkable similarity to the Old Red Sandstone of the Orcadian Basin in northeast Scotland'. Pirrie 2026 Conclusions: Clarke et al. (2024) 'proposed that it was derived from the Orcadian Basin of NE Scotland'. True as a report of the 2024 result.

claims.claim: Two years on, scientists still can't agree where it came from.
claims.source_checked: Clarke 2026 full text: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jqs.70080 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1002/jqs.70080); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/jqs.70080; Pirrie 2026 full text: https://www.lyellcollection.org/doi/full/10.1144/jgs2026-090 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1144/jgs2026-090); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1144/jgs2026-090; Parker Pearson 2024 full-text PDF: https://journals.uclpress.co.uk/ai/article/3293/galley/18572/download/ and article page journals.uclpress.co.uk/ai/article/id/3293/ (doi:10.14324/AI.27.1.13); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.14324/AI.27.1.13
claims.note: Clarke 2026 (online 4 Jun 2026) still proposes mainland NE Scotland, Caithness or Inverness-Black Isle 'the most likely source', while 'its source location within this large basin remains unresolved'. Pirrie 2026 (online 5 Nov 2026): 'detailed multi-proxy characterization of the Altar Stone raises questions over this interpretation'; scarce chrome spinel 'may indicate that an origin from this part of NE Scotland needs re-evaluating' (said of Clarke 2026's proposal); Conclusions 'the provenance of the Altar Stone has yet to be determined with confidence'. That is a published disagreement. Aug 2024 to Nov 2026 is about two years. 'Still' is fair: no source has been agreed at any point (Parker Pearson 2024 p.129 'As yet, the actual outcrop from which the Altar Stone was extracted is unknown').

claims.claim: Hook as a viewer who swipes at second two leaves it: 'In 2024, Stonehenge's Altar Stone was traced to Scotland' (A4)
claims.source_checked: Clarke 2024 full text: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07652-1?error=cookies_not_supported (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1; Clarke 2026 full text: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jqs.70080 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1002/jqs.70080); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/jqs.70080; Pirrie 2026 full text: https://www.lyellcollection.org/doi/full/10.1144/jgs2026-090 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1144/jgs2026-090); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1144/jgs2026-090
claims.note: The sentence is a dated report of a published result and is true. The belief it may leave (the stone is from Scotland) is the contested leading hypothesis, not something any source shows to be false: Clarke 2026 favours NE Scotland; Pirrie 2026 says the NE Scotland origin 'needs re-evaluating' and the provenance is 'as yet unknown', but neither excludes Scotland, and Pirrie's isotope data make 'an ORS provenance ... more likely than a Carboniferous source'. 'In 2024' frames it as a dated claim, and the next sentence (and the title) carry the dispute. Passes A4.

claims.note: Clarke 2024 dated zircon, apatite and rutile 'from two fragments of the Altar Stone' (MS3, 2010K.240); grains 'typically 10-40 µm wide' ('tiny').
